record.title: xAI says Grok Bot update adds credential Vault and broadens agent actions
record.summary: An October 23 changelog for Grok Bot v0.75.5 says Bots can store logins, payment cards and contact details in a Vault and fill them at sign-in or checkout. The update also adds email forwarding and says Auto Review asks less often for requested actions; requested email and Slack messages send after Auto Review allows them, while routine and other-turn sends remain drafts. These are vendor-described features, not independently tested outcomes. xAI documentation says payment confirmations still require user handoff and describes Auto Review as model-based.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: xAI’s October 23 Grok Bot v0.75.5 changelog says Bots can save logins, payment cards and contact information in a Vault and fill those details at sign-in or checkout; it also adds forwarding messages from a Bot’s own inbox.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The same changelog says Auto Review asks less often for actions requested in the user’s own words. It says user-requested email and Slack messages send after Auto Review allows them, while sends on routine and other turns remain drafts; a denied approval is not retried until another user message.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: Current xAI product documentation says Ask-first rules take precedence over automatic allowances, describes Auto Review as model-based, and says payment confirmations require user handoff.

claims.label: NOT_ESTABLISHED
claims.text: Independent testing of the release behavior, rollout by plan, adoption, unintended-send rate and security effectiveness was not established.

evidence_gaps.description: No independent test measured Vault field access, Auto Review approval decisions, email/Slack sending behavior or checkout/payment confirmation boundaries.
The changelog and docs do not establish which plans received every v0.75.5 feature or how widely users adopted them.

brief.importance_rationale: If implemented as described, combining stored login/payment credentials, outbound email actions and fewer approval prompts changes the practical authority boundary of a persistent agent. The evidence is a vendor changelog and documentation, with no independent behavior, adoption or outcome measurement.
limitations: All feature descriptions are vendor-reported; no independent implementation test or usage measurement was performed.
Account-plan rollout and broad availability are not established by the changelog.
xAI documentation describes Auto Review as model-based and recommends least privilege and explicit approval rules; this does not establish that those controls prevent all unintended side effects.

relationships.summary: The events concern distinct Grok releases: this Oct 23 update describes Grok Bot product actions and approval behavior; the Sep 21 record concerns Grok 4.7 model training and benchmark claims.

technical.claimed_result: xAI’s changelog says Grok Bot v0.75.5 adds Vault storage/fill for logins, payment cards and contact details and email forwarding. It says Auto Review asks less often for requested actions and permits user-requested email/Slack sending after review; routine and other-turn sends remain drafts.
technical.compute_or_cost: No compute, price, user uptake or operational cost result is reported in these release notes.
technical.demonstrated_result: The primary pages demonstrate that xAI published these feature and control descriptions. No independent test of the actual release behavior was conducted.
technical.mechanism: According to xAI’s changelog, users can save login, card and contact details in Vault for filling on sign-in or checkout. Auto Review evaluates actions before they run; the docs say Ask-first rules take precedence over automatic allowances and that payment confirmations are handed to the user.
technical.regime: Grok Bot product update v0.75.5 dated October 23, 2026. Vendor documentation says access and administrative controls vary by account and plan. The account covers announced product behavior, not a tested deployment, usage sample or model-performance evaluation.
technical.reproducibility: No independent behavior test or reproduction was available for this activation.
technical.strongest_baseline: No matched baseline or comparative evaluation is provided; the previous Grok Bot behavior is not independently described in this release note.

brief.title: xAI says Grok Bot update adds credential Vault and broadens agent actions
brief.why_it_matters: Credential storage and outbound messaging expand the actions a persistent assistant can take, while the update also changes how often a person sees an approval prompt. This changes the operational boundary worth evaluating; the current public account is based on vendor release notes and documentation, not an independent behavior or safety test.

other.title: xAI describes Grok 4.7's longer-horizon training and reports multi-hour task results
other.summary: In a September 21 release, xAI described Grok 4.7 as using a larger base than Grok 4.6, a longer reinforcement-learning run weighted toward harder multi-hour tasks, and training to understand the Grok Bot harness. The release reports Grok 4.7 scores across coding, office, terminal, legal, electrical-engineering and clinical benchmarks, including 37.6% on Terminal-Bench 4.0 versus 20.3% for Grok 4.6. These are company-reported results; the page does not provide test protocols, sample sizes or uncertainty.
